subject: Intermittent POST failures during private cutover — SNAT burst + MTU + SG checks
messages:
From: infra@haloedge.io
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: netops@haloedge.io, ops@haloedge.io
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: [ACTION] Intermittent POST failures after private cutover — need urgent help

Vanessa / Redwood team,

We cutover our private deployment to the Redwood VPC gateway at 03:00 UTC this morning. Most traffic is fine but we're seeing intermittent 5xx/connection reset on large POST uploads (50–250KB payloads) from our on-prem clients to the Redwood inference endpoint. Failures come in bursts and self-heal for a few minutes, then recur.

Symptoms we've observed: 
- Client logs show TCP retransmits and TLS handshake timeouts for certain flows.
- Traceroutes show one hop with ICMP fragmentation-needed responses for some clients.
- We captured server-side logs that show short-lived errors: "tcp_reset" and "write: short write" during bursts.

We've attached: haloedge_post_failures.pcap, traceroute-20261212.txt, and a snapshot of our conntrack table (snat-conntrack-snapshot-1212.log).

We suspect a combination of ephemeral SNAT exhaustion during bursts + MTU fragmentation and possibly a security group or firewall dropping fragments when asymmetry occurs. Can your network team triage? This is impacting a small subset of production customers.

Urgent details:
- Time window: first seen 02:55–03:35 UTC; recurring at ~06:10 UTC
- Affected client subnets: 10.44.0.0/16 (on-prem NATed to a small egress pool)
- Endpoint: private-infer-us-west.redwood.internal:443 (mapped via our peering)

Thanks,
Paul Herrera
Infra Lead, HaloEdge
infra@haloedge.io

Paul — thanks for the detailed packet captures and conntrack dump. Sorry you're seeing this during cutover. I'm looping in Jonas (network/solutions) and Marissa (AM) to coordinate on remediation and customer comms.

Initial asks so we can triage quickly: 
1) Can you confirm whether your egress NAT pool is a single /29 vs. multiple /24s (we saw a small pool in the conntrack snapshot).
2) Do the failing clients share the same NAT IP? If so, do they send bursts concurrently (e.g., batch workers)?
3) Are you using MSS clamping on your edge devices? The traceroute shows ICMP fragmentation-needed for MTU 1400 on one path.

Jonas — can you prioritize a packet review? I flagged INF-1324 in Jira and attached the captures to the ticket. Marissa will coordinate customer notices.

I'll be on the bridge in 20 minutes.

—Vanessa

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, infra@haloedge.io
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 10:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: [ACTION] Intermittent POST failures after private cutover — packet notes + quick tests

Thanks for the loop. Quick read of the pcap + conntrack snapshot shows two likely contributors (both can interact):

1) SNAT slot churn / ephemeral port starvation: Your conntrack snapshot shows ~23k TCP entries on a single external NAT IP. Many entries are TIME_WAIT/ESTABLISHED churn during the burst. If your egress pool is small (e.g., single /29), concurrent clients easily exhaust source ports and mappings get expired/overwritten which causes mid-flow connection resets on the server side.

2) MTU fragmentation + path MTU discovery (PMTUD) loss: I can see multiple "ICMP frag needed" with DF=1 for MSS ~1460, followed by retransmits. If fragments are being dropped anywhere (some middlebox or SG configured to deny fragmented packets), the client's PMTUD fails and larger POSTs stall/timeout. The traceroute you provided includes a hop that responds with MTU 1400; your clients' stacks may be sending larger packets without MSS clamping.

Additionally: there are a handful of flows where outbound responses take a different egress NAT IP (asymmetry) — one side uses a different SNAT address than the incoming mapping. If Redwood's routing chooses a different egress for the return, stateful SGs or firewalls could drop those packets.

Immediate mitigations to try (low-risk):
- Expand egress NAT pool on your edge (add at least 2 more public IPs) for the cutover period to reduce port reuse.
- Enable MSS clamping (MSS 1360) on your on-prem edge to avoid PMTUD reliance.
- On Redwood side, we'll verify that our return path keeps SNAT mappings sticky for peer prefixes and ensure our egress selectors prefer the same path for the established session.

Paul: can you run a quick test for me? From a failing client host, run: 
- curl -v --raw --limit-rate 200k --max-time 30 https://private-infer-us-west.redwood.internal/health/upload (attach logs)
- tcpdump -ni any host <redwood-peer-ip> and capture 60s around a failing POST.

I'll stay on the bridge. If we confirm SNAT/port exhaustion + MTU, we should plan a remediation playbook and a short partial rollback option (route a small percentage of traffic via a different peering hop while you expand the pool).

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 11:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: [ACTION] Intermittent POST failures after private cutover — packet notes + quick tests

Jonas / Vanessa — thanks. Quick answers: 
- Egress pool is a single /29 (we were trying to keep IP footprint small during beta).
- Failing clients do share the same NAT IP — the workers in our ingestion fleet burst in parallel during morning processing windows.
- No MSS clamping enabled previously.

We ran your suggested curl test from a failing host and attached the tcpdump (excerpted). The pcap shows repeated TCP retransmits and ICMP frag-needed responses for MSS ~1448, then a server-side RST when conntrack mapping appears to be reused. Attaching: haloedge_post_failures.pcap (full) and traceroute output.

Immediate action from our side: expanding egress pool to /28 now (T-15m). Enabling MSS clamp at 1360 on our edge devices now (T-10m).

Can Redwood confirm: will you apply any sticky-egress preference for HaloEdge peer prefixes to avoid return-path asymmetry while we expand the pool? That sticky behavior would reduce the time window of failures.

Thanks — we'll keep you posted.

Paul Herrera
Infra Lead, HaloEdge

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: infra@haloedge.io, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 13 Dec 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: [RESOLVED?] Intermittent POST failures — mitigation applied and next steps

Quick update after the changes: 
- HaloEdge expanded to a /28 and enabled MSS 1360. We observed reduced retransmits and zero RSTs in the follow-up capture you sent.
- On Redwood side we pinned egress selection for HaloEdge peer prefixes to the same ECMP bucket used for the handshake for 5 minutes (sticky behavior) and verified conntrack behavior — no asymmetry during the test window.

Root cause (summary): small egress NAT pool caused ephemeral port exhaustion during bursty client behavior, which combined with PMTUD failures (no MSS clamp) and a transient asymmetry in return path selection. The combination caused in-flight connections to be reset or dropped. Security groups were not intentionally dropping fragments, but stateful rules did enforce established state and thus dropped returns when asymmetric egress occurred.

Recommendations / next steps: 
- HaloEdge to keep the /28 pool for production and monitor ephemeral port utilization for 48–72 hours.
- Maintain MSS clamping at 1360 for on-prem edges to avoid fragmentation for the foreseeable term.
- Redwood will make the sticky-egress selection for peer prefixes configurable in the Console (INF-1324) so customers can enable it during cutovers.
- We'll coordinate a short postmortem and update the cutover runbook with explicit NAT pool sizing guidance and an MSS check.

Marissa will draft the customer advisory and schedule a 30-minute postmortem next week. Paul, let us know if you want Redwood to assist with any rollback plan.

Thanks everyone — great coordination.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
